subject: Post-call: scaling handoff & burst hypotheses
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@parcelport.com>, Tim Luo <tim@fastlane.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: scaling handoff & burst hypotheses

Thanks again for the call earlier — short recap and proposed next steps so we can get the sizing handoff to our performance team. I tried to capture the constraints you emphasized and a couple of hypotheses we want to validate with the sample telemetry you offered.

Key constraints / targets from today
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 350ms for single-turn (non-stream) generative requests; streaming tail target 99th <= 1.2s for chunked updates.
- Steady-state throughput: ~18-25 QPS on average during business hours.
- Peak bursts: short crest events up to ~500-700 QPS for ~10s (observed during checkout spikes).
- Average prompt + completion token envelope: ~420 tokens/request (prompt ~120, completion ~300) — please flag if that's off.
- Concurrency: up to ~1.5k concurrent connections in burst windows; many are streaming sessions (estimated ~55% streaming).

Hypotheses we will size against (what Redwood will run in the sizing worksheet)
1) If average tokens/request is 420 and average completion is 300, then peak token/sec during crest (700 QPS) ~210k tokens/sec.
2) Streaming sessions amortize per-token latency differently — we may recommend separate streaming capacity + slotting to keep cold start minimal.
3) A small prefix-caching policy for repeated system prompts could reduce token load by 8-12% on your top two flows.

Attachments / data request
- You mentioned a 10-minute sample of telemetry showing both burst events and steady baseline — please attach anything with timestamps, token counts, and a flag for streaming vs non-streaming. (I expect a ndjson or CSV with fields: ts, qps, avg_tokens, streaming_pct).
- We've attached a lightweight sizing template (redwood_sizing_template.xlsx) — fill in the highlighted rows when you can.

Immediate next steps
- Elaine: share the 10-min telemetry sample + any short-run logs for a typical checkout peak (by EOD Wed).
- Karthik/Neha: I'll let you two take the sizing pass once data is in; propose a 45-minute sizing sync on Thurs to walk assumptions.
- Tim: if you want, share any historical retention rules that affect token replay/trace volumes.

Thanks — I'll consolidate numbers and post the back-of-envelope before the sync.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0143

From: Elaine Park <elaine@parcelport.com>

Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 17:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: scaling handoff & burst hypotheses

Thanks Monica — this looks right at a high level. Quick clarifications:
- Average tokens/request: our telemetry shows median ~380 but 75th ~500 during content-heavy checkouts. Use 420 as a good representative average.
- Burst: our busiest crest last month reached ~680 QPS for ~9s, so 700 is a safe upper bound.
- Streaming: ~58% of sessions are streaming (users see intermediary suggestions while typing).

I've attached a 10-min extract (parcelport_telemetry_sample.ndjson) taken from last week's morning spike and a short README. The file includes per-second qps and token counts and a boolean for streaming.

Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of SRE, ParcelPort
elaine@parcelport.com

Attachment: parcelport_telemetry_sample.ndjson (10MB sample, per-second rows)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: scaling handoff & burst hypotheses

Thanks both — quick follow-ups before I start the sizing pass:
1) For streaming sessions: are you sending single-token deltas (server push) or batched frames every 200–500ms? That affects effective per-connection CPU.
2) Concurrency number: Monica noted ~1.5k concurrent connections in bursts. Is that concurrent open websockets, or concurrent in-flight token-generation calls (i.e., RPCs to the model)?
3) Any SLA differences across customer tiers we should model (e.g., gold tier gets lower max-latency target)?

If you can answer 1–3 briefly I can lock down kernel/instance selection and give a rough fleet estimate by EOD.

—Karthik

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Elaine Park <elaine@parcelport.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 11:30:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: scaling handoff & burst hypotheses

Taking a first pass with the sample Elaine sent. Back-of-envelope assumptions I used:
- Representative avg tokens/request = 420 (Elaine confirmed median ~380, 75th ~500).
- Peak crest = 700 QPS for 10s.
- Token/sec at peak = 700 QPS * 420 tokens = 294,000 tokens/sec.
- If 58% streaming and streaming average generation rate ~0.9 token/sec (interactive), then sustained streaming token/sec adds ~0.58 * concurrent_sessions * 0.9 — which for 1.5k concurrent translates to ~783 tokens/sec (negligible vs crest token rate, but affects concurrency/slotting).

Immediate implications:
- Peak token/sec dominates compute sizing; we'll need quantized model variant or increased kernel concurrency to keep 95th latency under 350ms on single-turn requests.
- Suggestion: run two slot classes — "interactive streaming" slots optimized for low per-token tail vs "burst batch" slots for non-stream generation. This reduces cost by allowing different instance types.

I'll produce a short worksheet with two scenario rows (conservative / optimistic) and send it to the Drive link in ~2 hours. Karthik — I need your confirmation on whether we should assume 100% greenfield routing to Redwood or a hybrid fallback to an on-prem variant during crests.

-Neha

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@parcelport.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Tim Luo <tim@fastlane.inference>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: scaling handoff & burst hypotheses

Great progress — thanks for the telemetry, Elaine, and the fast sizing pass, Neha. Quick confirmation of next steps and owners: 
- Neha: upload the two-scenario worksheet to the Drive link and add a short note on slot-class mapping (due: Fri EOD PT).
- Karthik: draft the instance-class recommendation (quantized model vs more instances) and include cost delta for both conservative/optimistic rows (due: Mon 10 Aug).
- Elaine / ParcelPort: confirm whether you're comfortable with greenfield routing to Redwood for the pilot or prefer hybrid; if hybrid, share any capacity constraints for the fallback path.
- Monica (me): schedule the 45-minute sizing sync the week of Aug 9th — I'll send a Doodle in the morning.

We'll aim to run a 1-week pilot with two route variants (streaming-optimized + burst-optimized) once the worksheet and routing choice are confirmed. I'll also attach the HubSpot deal link and the Drive folder for shared docs.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Monica
